newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end short session sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end short session sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended a shortened trading session sharply higher and just below new six-month highs as attention once again turned to the upside.
September Treasury bond futures shot upward near the opening and barely glanced back, ratcheting progressively higher during the day on spurts of big dealer buying.
The only hiccup in the market's move higher occurred late in the morning, when brokers reported that a cash player sold some $500 million in principal-only bond strips.
"That took the luster off" the futures' rally, a T-bond futures floor broker said of the cash sales.
"That knocked the market down four or five ticks," another floor broker said of the sales, rumored to be Keogh-related.
Futures otherwise rallied on heavy turnover, brokers in the long and short ends said.
"There was major-league institutional buying in bonds," said the second broker, adding that the rally appeared fueled by fresh buying. "There's a lot of money to put to work."

She said one dealer "got the ball rolling" as the June U.S. jobs data were released when it bought 5,000 September T-bonds. Another dealer bought 6,000 to 8,000 contracts during the kneejerk rally up to the early-morning high at 113-03/32.
Other dealers and institutions soon swooped in, scooping up 500-lots at a shot all the way up, she added.
"That report was not overly bullish," she said of the June employment figures. "But it gave people the green light that the economy is not moving faster than anyone thought."

Nonfarm payrolls in June rose 217,000 versus forecasts for up 222,000. May's rise was revised to 166,000 from the originally reported 138,000. Joblessness last month rose to 5.0 percent compared to forecasts for a steady, 4.8-percent rate.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.3 percent to $12.22 versus forecasts for a 0.4 percent rise.

"There was very good volume, especially in options and in spreads," said a Eurodollar floor broker. She said the same dealer that bought up to 8,000 September T-bonds also was seen buying at least 12,000 September/December Eurodollar spreads.

The buying spree hoisted September T-bonds to a peak at 113-15/32, its highest price since last December. The contract easily hurdled stiff resistance, such as the June 20 peak of 112-24/32, and broke out on the upside, technicians said.
In the short end, December Eurodollars closed above the key 93.99 level, giving a measuring objective at 94.13, the Eurodollar broker added.
"Technically, you're closing on a very positive note in Euros and in bonds," she said.
Some technicians looked for the next upside target in September T-bonds in the low- to mid-114 area.
"The next stop is 114-08/09," added the first T-bond broker.
Debt futures are closed Friday for U.S. Independence Day.

September T-bonds settled up 1-04/32 at 113-06/32, 10-year notes rose 22/32 to 109-04/32, munis gained 30/32 to 118-21/32, December T-bills added 0.08 to 94.725, and December Eurodollars gained 0.08 to 94.045. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
